pass_b_english: Through faith in Christ, we experience forgiveness of sin, and with it, a gift and grace of the Holy Spirit, a dignity of adoption, an enjoyment of unending good things, and a hope of the kingdom of heaven, where there is certainly joy, and fleeing from pain, sorrow, and groaning.

In this state, we can rejoice, free from pain, sorrow, and groaning, because there is no cause at all for groaning and pain, and hope prevails, and joy, cheerfulness, unshakeable confidence, and joy abound.

The Lord says, 'I am, I am the one comforting you.', which means he is the one giving all spiritual comfort, and bearing with the helps to be well, to walk with good courage on the path of all virtue.
We must recognize our true nature and not fear mortal men, and the son of man, who have withered like grass.
We must not forget God, who created us, heaven, and earth, and instead, we should always fear the face of the one afflicting us.
For as he planned to lift you up, his anger will not stand, nor will it delay, for in your being saved, he will not stand, nor will he delay.
The Lord's statement, 'I am,' is a declaration of his eternal existence, and he is indeed the One Who Is, being life itself, not receiving existence from another, nor having it as a gift.
This dignity is godlike and extraordinary, for it is in the nature beyond all things to be and to live.
Perhaps, in these things, there is also a measure of encouragement, and you will come to understand in a different way.

The Savior, through the evangelical proclamations, called people to the forgiveness of sin, which comes through faith in him, and to the partaking of the Holy Spirit, and to the boast and glory of adoption, with a hope of the kingdom of heaven, and the need to rejoice.
However, Israel, you did not look down on the one who exists, and you despised the one who calls to life, fearing instead a mortal man and the son of a man, who have withered like grass.
You forgot the God who made you, who established the heaven and founded the earth, and you feared the face of the one who oppresses you.
God blames the teachers of the Jews, who have opposed the glory of the Savior until now, and have not proclaimed at all the one who came to them.
He worked many wonders, but they held bitter words of blasphemy, saying that he cast out demons in Beelzebub, the ruler of the demons.
With teachings beyond the law, he often convicted those who listened, but they fell into impiety, so that they were against those who praised.
This dignity is godlike and extraordinary, for it is in the nature beyond all things to be and to live, as noted in the scholion 70.1128.
As the Lord says, 'Know what you are, and do not fear mortal man, and the son of man, who have withered like grass (Isaiah 51:12).'
And, 'Forget not God who made you, who made heaven and founded the earth (Isaiah 51:13).'
And, 'Fear always the face of the one afflicting you (Isaiah 51:13).'
